svg.text: AWS US-East-1 Identity Center & Console Outage Architecture
Localized us-east-1 network issue, IAM Identity Center console lockout, and service degradation (Nov 15, 2026)

g.text: 1. Cell Degradation
Hypothesis
us-east-1 Network Issue
AWS confirmed network issue in us-east-1
triggered elevated error rates starting at 03:05 PST.
Network Load Balancer and IAM Identity Center
endpoints experienced elevated error rates and latency.
Existing workload impact was not fully disclosed.
Cross-Cell Synchronous Coupling
Model: Frontend proxies hold cross-cell dependencies
into localized token-signing backend microservices.
Degraded network path slows inter-cell socket reads.
Worker threads block waiting for remote responses.
Demonstrates cell boundary blast-radius risks.
Ingress Worker Pool Starvation
Edge ingress threads exhausted during socket timeouts.
Worker pool capacity for new connections drops to 0%.
Console login requests dropped or queued at edge.
Console users observe HTTP 500 / 504 timeouts.
93-minute delay before public health dashboard update.
2. Control Plane Stall
Cascade
Worldwide Console Lockout
Engineers unable to authenticate to AWS Console.
Some IAM Identity Center sign-ins failed.
Impact on individual CI/CD role calls was not detailed.
AWS Sign Up for new tenant accounts failed.
DevOps incident response severely hampered.
11 Dependent Services Degraded
Some services relying on Identity Center were affected.
AWS did not identify STS timeouts as the cause.
Amazon Connect authentication was affected.
Individual cross-service effects were not detailed.
Telemetry delays compounded operator confusion.
Running Workloads Kept Running
Existing workload impact depends on dependencies.
Cached credentials may remain valid until expiry.
AWS did not assess every customer workload.
NLB connectivity in one cell was also affected.
The status update did not assess cyber attribution.
3. Cell Resolution
Resolution
Authentication Mitigation (05:20 PST)
AWS mitigated core authentication failures at 05:20.
Console sign-in error rates returned to normal levels.
Regional engineers addressed degraded network paths.
Remaining NLB issues resolved subsequently at 06:21.
Active duration totaled 3 hours 16 minutes.
05:20 PST Auth; 06:21 PST NLB Resolved
05:20 PST: AWS reported auth issue mitigated.
Console login error rates returned to normal.
06:21 PST: Remaining NLB issues fully resolved.
AWS reported services operating normally.
Active infrastructure impact ended in 3h 16m.
06:53 PST Resolved Update Posted
AWS posted final "Resolved" status update.
Total active duration: 3 hours 16 minutes.
Weekend timing blunted consumer impact.
AWS faced critique over 93m initial alert lag.
Internal root cause was not disclosed in the update.
4. Engineering Safeguards & Cell Isolation Architecture
Cell Isolation & Sub-Second Circuit Breaking
1. Strict Cell-Boundary Enforcement: Prevent cross-zone RPC dependencies
so a degraded cell cannot starve thread pools in healthy availability zones.
2. Aggressive RPC Timeouts: Clamp token-signing socket reads to 500ms
with rapid circuit-tripping to drop dead nodes before worker pools deplete.
3. Automated Regional Failover: Identity Center endpoints must seamlessly
fail over between cells without manual operator intervention.
4. Decoupled Token Cache: Serve cached role metadata during transient
network stalls to keep existing authenticated sessions operational.
Prevents regional control-plane cascades during localized hardware failures.
Enterprise Break-Glass Playbook
1. Direct IAM Emergency Credentials: Maintain break-glass IAM users with
hardware MFA that bypass IAM Identity Center during global SSO outages.
2. Multi-Region STS Endpoints: Configure SDK clients to use regional STS
endpoints (e.g. sts.us-west-2.amazonaws.com) rather than global us-east-1.
3. Automated Edge Health Probing: Surface real-time console login latency
on status dashboards without manual engineering approval delays.
4. Extended Session Expiration: Allow DevOps sessions to persist for 12 hours
to shield active incident responders from short-lived token refresh outages.
Guarantees continuous operator access during critical cloud degradations.
